months.2: Temperatures remain cool, making this a good time for low-elevation coastal walks.
months.5: This is a prime month for walking, with long, clear days and comfortable temperatures for long mountain routes.
months.7: High summer heat makes long walking difficult. Stick to short, shaded walks or early morning coastal paths.

scottish-highlands-skye.overview: The Scottish Highlands and the Isle of Skye offer dramatic walking, defined by deep glens, rugged coastlines, and jagged peaks. Day hikers head to routes like the Quiraing landslip and the Old Man of Storr, where steep, rocky paths lead to sweeping views of the sea and moors. Multi-day walkers can tackle the 96-mile West Highland Way through the mainland valleys. The best conditions run from May to September, though the middle of the year brings notorious biting midges.

months.1: Freezing temperatures, snow on the heights, and very short daylight hours limit options. High routes need winter skills, leaving walkers to low-level glen and coastal paths.
months.2: Cold, wet weather and short days keep walkers to low-level glens and coastal paths, with snow lingering on the high ground.
months.12: Short days and freezing temperatures settle in, with snow on the heights. Low-level glen and coastal paths are the practical options.
months.7: The ridges stay accessible with very long days. Midges are at their worst on still, damp days in the glens, so a breeze and a head net help.

seoul.overview: Seoul is a major city with real mountain hiking right on its subway lines. Bukhansan National Park offers steep, rocky day hikes to granite peaks, with the steep climb to Baegundae rewarding walkers with views over the metropolis. Closer to the center, the Seoul City Wall traces the ridges of Bugaksan and Namsan on paved paths and stairs. The best walking is in the clear, mild weather of spring and fall.

months.7: The monsoon season brings heavy, frequent rain and high humidity. Trails in Bukhansan can be slick and muddy, and the heat makes the climbing tiring.

sequoia-kings-canyon.overview: Sequoia and Kings Canyon offer two distinct hiking worlds: the giant sequoia groves and the rugged High Sierra. Day hikers can walk among the massive trees on the Congress Trail or climb the granite dome of Moro Rock for panoramic views of the Great Western Divide. Trekkers come for multi-day routes like the 41.4-mile Rae Lakes Loop or the High Sierra Trail, which crosses the mountain range to Mount Whitney. The high alpine routes require wilderness permits and are only clear of snow from mid-summer to early fall.

months.1: Winter walking and snowshoeing dominate. The high country is buried in snow, but trails in the Giant Forest and Grant Grove offer snowshoe routes among the massive trees.
months.7: The High Sierra opens completely. The Rae Lakes Loop and High Sierra Trail are clear, with spectacular alpine lakes and granite peaks, though afternoon thunderstorms are common.

months.2: Etna holds deep snow at elevation, limiting walking to the lower slopes or snowshoe routes. Coastal and lowland trails are green, though rain is common.
months.4: An excellent month for walking. Wildflowers bloom along the coastal paths, and temperatures are comfortable for long hikes. Etna's snow line recedes, opening more of the volcano.

snowdonia.overview: Walking in Wales centers on Snowdonia, with the rugged peaks of Snowdon, the Glyderau, and the Carneddau. Hikers can tackle the steep Watkin Path with its 3,300-foot climb to the summit of Snowdon, or take the classic Pyg and Miners' tracks past high mountain lakes. The best conditions run from April to October, as winter brings serious ice and snow to the heights.

months.5: Longer daylight and warming temperatures make this an excellent time for demanding ascents in the Glyderau. The high ridges are generally clear of snow.
months.9: Early autumn brings crisp air and excellent visibility for summit hikes. The high routes remain clear, making it a great time for big mountain days.

southeast-alaska.overview: Hiking here means walking into deep coastal rainforests and up to glacier views, often starting right from the port towns. Juneau offers the steep, unmaintained West Glacier Trail for a close look at the ice, while Skagway is the start of the Chilkoot Trail, a 33-mile, multi-day trek over the historic gold rush pass. The season is short, driven by snowmelt, with trails at their best from June to August.

months.5: The hiking season opens as the cruise ships arrive. Lower trails clear of snow, while the higher routes and the Chilkoot Trail pass still hold snow.
months.6: Summer hiking is in full swing. The Chilkoot Trail opens for permitted trekkers, and the West Glacier Trail is clear enough for a steep day hike, though rain is always possible.

months.1: The dry weather makes this prime time for the hill country. The Adam's Peak trail is fully open for night ascents, and paths around Ella and the Knuckles range are clear.
months.2: Dry, settled weather continues, with clear sunrise views from Adam's Peak and firm paths around Ella and the Knuckles range.
months.3: Dry weather lasts, though heat builds by midday. The Adam's Peak climb and the Ella Rock trails are best done early.
months.6: Heavy monsoon rain hits the central highlands and southwest, leaving many hill trails waterlogged and wrapped in low cloud.
months.7: The rains continue, with opportunistic breaks in the weather the only chance for the hill trails, which stay waterlogged and obscured by low cloud.
months.8: Heavy rains keep the hill trails waterlogged, and low cloud hides the viewpoints for much of the time.
months.10: The inter-monsoonal period brings unpredictable rain across the island. Hikes need flexible timing, as afternoon downpours are common around Ella and the Knuckles range.
months.11: Inter-monsoon rain continues, with afternoon downpours common on the trails around Ella and the Knuckles range. Mornings are the best window.

svalbard.overview: Hiking in Svalbard means guided day walks across open tundra and glaciers, often reached by boat from Longyearbyen. Because of polar bears, anyone leaving the settlement must carry a means of scaring them off, and most walkers go with an armed guide. The short summer window offers stark Arctic scenery, from steep climbs up local peaks like Sarkofagen to remote shorelines.

sydney.overview: Sydney offers coastal paths and nearby mountain trails accessible by train or a short drive. The walking ranges from easy harbor routes to the long 16-mile Coast Track in Royal National Park. Inland, the Blue Mountains provide dramatic sandstone cliffs and deep valleys, with popular day hikes like the Grand Canyon track and the Three Sisters walk.

months.6: June brings cooler temperatures, ideal for steep ascents in the Blue Mountains without the intense heat of earlier months.
